topics.topic: Module boundaries and contracts for configuration, startup, and backup
questions: What are the module boundaries and dependable results or failures for loading settings, validating startup, creating or opening the store, opening listeners, scheduling backup runs, making and checking a backup, retention cleanup and reporting the newest kept backup?

quotes:
In order: `configuration.load_configuration`;
`backups.probe_backup_location`; `store.open_store`; the owner interface's
listener and then, unless the start is owner-only, the service API's, each
at its address in the loaded configuration (A17 rule 1); then the surfaces answer; then two
passes: `owner_sessions.end_expired_sessions` every imported
`SESSION_PASS_SECONDS` and, except in an owner-only start,
`backups.run_daily_backup_if_due` every imported `BACKUP_LOOK_SECONDS`, each
from the start as Conventions, "Passes", says.

Nothing is served until every check passed; a listener that cannot be
opened closes the one already opened and has `store.discard_new_store`
remove a store this start made new (A17 rule 2); a restart ends every owner
session (A13 rule 2). It decides no check.

When due: the temporary files removed; a backup — the copy of
`store.copy_store_snapshot` encrypted with the key, its record holding the
instant, the release from the imported `RELEASE_VERSION` constant, the last
sequence number and the key's digest — checked by decrypting it and asking
`store.check_store_file`, and kept under a name made from its instant; the
backups older than 30 × 24 hours and the unreadable kept files deleted.
judgement.why: The startup coordinator, configuration, store and backup contracts state their ownership, ordering, dependable results, cleanup, scheduling, checking, retention and newest-backup behaviour.

precedent.topic: State 5 obligation for withdrawal manifest metadata
quotes:
In Registry's derived manifest record (R0-78), adding a room, publishing a
pointer and withdrawing one are `state-transition`. Each such write of the
agent waits for the owner's approval of its exact request, unless the owner
gave that flow version a standing approval for the node (K-08). A request for
access stays `draft-write`: it changes no access, replaces the session's
earlier request (R0-47) and is itself a question to the owner.

R0-78's idempotency key belongs to the writes whose retry could make a
second record (R0-36): adding a room and publishing a pointer carry one
(State 2 A01, R0-88). Withdrawing a pointer makes nothing; it names the
pointer only and carries no idempotency key, and a repeated withdrawal is
refused as withdrawing a pointer already withdrawn (Primary actions, R0-14).
Its replay behaviour in the manifest record is that a repeat is refused.
precedent.why: R0-99 already declares withdrawal's effect class, absence of an idempotency key, and replay refusal in the derived manifest record.

questions: What are the public obligations for registering and ending a session, reading access, requesting access, granting, declining, revoking, changing or clearing the active project, and owner-ending a session, including access-version inputs, indistinguishable not-found refusals and removal effects?

quotes:
Draft of 2026-11-01. The operations of `owner_sessions`, which hold the
owner's runtime state and never touch the store, and of `agent_sessions`,
which keep the agent sessions' records. Every one follows
`50_public_apis_0_conventions.md`.

The transaction; the session; the stated access version; decline or grant
with the picked project and whether to make it active; what
`projects.validate_project_reference` answered for it.

Stages (3) to (6): an unknown session or project; a stale version (A12 rule
3); a request no longer pending, an archived project (R0-70). A project
already in the set adds nothing, and the answer still clears the request.

An unregistered session, a project outside the set and no active project
when none is named are one answer, as a project that does not exist, and it
hides every later failure (A10 rule 3); checked in the call's own
transaction, so a revocation holds from the next call (A10 rules 5, 6); a
session's own operations — reading its access, requesting access, ending it
— need only the registered session.
judgement.why: The agent_sessions contracts cover registration, access reads and requests, grants, declines, revocation, active-project changes and ending, including version inputs, indistinguishable refusals and removal effects.

quotes:
`module:artifact_pointers`. Publish a pointer of a declared type with a

The transaction; the project; the type; `uri`, `payload_ref` or both; the

The pointer as it stands, with every fact 'list artifacts' answers for it —

the request id among this project's pointers, project and publisher among the facts — a

topics.topic: Public contracts for project and customer record operations
questions: What do callers supply and what may they rely on for project and customer creation, reads, lists, corrections, lifecycle transitions, erasures, validation, context, billing data and agent projection, including revisions, disclosure refusals, no-op results and atomic effects?

quotes:
Draft of 2026-11-01. The operations of `customers`, `projects` and
`artifact_pointers`, which own the Customer, the Project with its Object and
Rooms, and the ArtifactPointer. Every one follows
`50_public_apis_0_conventions.md`.

A transition to the state a record is in answers the record
  unchanged with `changed: false` (A05); a create's repeat answers the
  existing record with `changed: false` (A01 rule 4). Every operation that
  may be accepted without a change — a repeat, an equal correction, a
  transition to the state a record is in — answers `changed`, because
  `operations` appends the entry and mints a confirmation id only when it
  changed state (A14 rules 1, 3, 5); one that changes state whenever it is
  accepted answers no `changed`.

The mark set or cleared, an end dated as given or today; the revision and
last-changed instant move. A transition to the state it is in changes
nothing, and ending an ended relationship with another date does not move it
(A05 rules 1, 3).
Every change the step made is committed together, or none is.
judgement.why: The customer and project public_op sections specify their inputs, outputs, refusals and effects, while the shared conventions fix unchanged repeats, audit consequences and transaction atomicity.

author_guidance: Before editing, identify the decision's owning state from the phase purpose, question_scope and layer obligations, then choose a disposition for each topic that awaits one.
fixed: repair a decision the owning state must make; do not add later-layer implementation choices merely to close a topic. Record the fix commit and review the changed text once.

carried: name the receiving layer and use --what to preserve the choice, its options and consequences, and the required guarantee every option must keep. Decide any guarantee owned here before carrying its execution onward.
accepted: explain why the remaining choice is permitted. Bring an unresolved product choice to the owner with its options and consequences; absence of a quoted requirement does not decide it.
contradiction and standard_violation take no disposition: repair the offending text in its owning state and review the change. Deterministic transition findings must also close through their checks.
State 5: decide obligations between modules for inputs, results, failures and effects; leave exact contract forms and hidden implementation to later layers.
